item.description: Missing URL parsing implementation in base plugin class. Many tests fail because URL parsing methods are not properly implemented or returning unexpected values in plugin classes that inherit from NotifyBase.
item.contract: Plugins must implement proper URL parsing behavior that correctly handles URL schemes, authentication, and parameters according to their specific protocol specifications. The URL parsing should validate and extract all required components (user, password, host, port, path, query parameters) and store them appropriately for use in notification processing.

item.description: Asynchronous notification handling is broken. Tests like test_apprise_async indicate problems with async notification processing and event loop management.
item.contract: The Apprise class must properly support asynchronous notification processing through async_notify method that correctly manages event loops and coroutine handling throughout the notification flow. The async_notify method should be equivalent to the sync notify method but operate asynchronously.

item.description: Nextcloud plugin integration issues with HTTP request handling, authentication, and response parsing. Multiple Nextcloud-related tests fail due to incorrect HTTP client interaction.
item.contract: The Nextcloud plugin must properly handle HTTP requests with correct authentication, error handling, and response parsing. It should correctly process HTTP responses and handle edge cases like empty responses or exceptions during request processing.

item.description: Incorrect enum handling for notification types (NotifyType). Tests fail due to inconsistent enum values being returned from plugins.
item.contract: All plugins must consistently return proper NotifyType enum values that match the expected enum definitions. The enum handling should be standardized across all plugins to ensure consistent behavior.

item.description: Plugin initialization and registration issues. Some tests fail because plugins aren't being properly initialized or registered in the plugin manager.
item.contract: The plugin manager must correctly initialize and register all plugins upon startup. All plugins should be available for instantiation through the Apprise class and should be properly discoverable via the plugin manager.
